subject: Streaming fragmentation causing increased 5xx and latency
messages:
From: Kate Morris <kate@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 5xx + high latency from streaming since SDK v1.4.2

Marcus —

Since we upgraded to the client SDK v1.4.2 on 2026-09-09 we've observed a big uptick in 5xx responses and long tail latency on our streaming endpoints. Rough stats from our side (last 24h): error rate up to 6.8% (was ~0.3%), p95 latency jumping from 280ms to 1.6s, several timeouts in our streaming parser.

We run in-house transformers through your hosted endpoint; we didn't change server-side configs. Reverting to the old SDK reduced but did not eliminate the issue. Attaching a condensed log and a small capture. Can you confirm whether anything changed on your end or if you know of client-side parsing issues with the new SDK?

Attachments: support_log_0910.zip (log snippet + tcp captures)

Thanks,
Kate Morris
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Robotics
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Morris <kate@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xx + high latency from streaming since SDK v1.4.2

Kate — thanks for the heads-up and the logs. Sorry you're seeing this in production. I've looped in Monica (solutions) and Neha (eng) so we can triage quickly.

First quick asks to help scope:
- Can you confirm the exact SDK package name and checksum you deployed? (v1.4.2-rc2 or v1.4.2 stable?)
- Are you using the default streaming parser included in the SDK, or a custom framing layer?
- If you can share a short curl-based repro that triggers the failure we can run it in our staging.

As an immediate mitigation, you can temporarily switch to the non-streaming endpoint (blocking generation) via the query param ?stream=false — that should avoid the parser path entirely while we investigate. We will also look at server-side changes and rolling back any recent runtime updates if needed.

I've created internal ticket JIRA-INF-4821 and uploaded your log capture.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Kate Morris <kate@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Sep 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xx + high latency from streaming since SDK v1.4.2

Kate / Marcus — I pulled the zip and ran our parser against the tcp capture. Quick findings: several of the failed requests show truncated HTTP chunk headers in the stream frames (we see lines like "

" where a chunk-size line should be). That pattern leads our streaming reassembly code to drop remaining frames and surface a 502/504 back to the client.

Hypothesis: a client-side parser that aggressively trims carriage returns when converting frames into strings can remove the chunk-length line. The SDK v1.4.2 changed the framing buffer boundary logic (small perf patch) — if a consumer uses a non-bytes-safe parser, this change can expose a race where header fragments get lost.

I added a minimal repro and instructions here: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/repro/INF-4821 (repro_steps.txt attached). Repro steps assume a short-lived multi-chunk response from our staging model.

Immediate suggestions:
- As Marcus suggested, flip to ?stream=false for critical endpoints until we push a fix.
- Downgrade the client SDK to v1.4.1 if you must keep streaming enabled; that removes the buffer boundary change.
- On our side, we'll push a defensive reassembly patch that tolerates missing CRLFs between chunk headers and reparse more conservatively. ETA for a server-side patch: 48 hours (we'll try to expedite to 24).

Attachment: repro_steps.txt

Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Mike Conway <mike@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Kate Morris <kate@acme.com>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@acme.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2026 07:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xx + high latency from streaming since SDK v1.4.2

Marcus / Redwood —

This is impacting our customer SLAs. We need a firm mitigation plan and timeline. Please confirm by EOD PT today: 1) whether you can toggle a server-side safeguard for our account (rate-limit-friendly reassembly) 2) whether you can push a hotfix that accepts fragmented headers for our tenant only 3) if not possible, confirm rollback options.

We have a production run tomorrow and cannot risk another outage. Kate has already flipped a few non-critical endpoints to non-streaming, but going forward we need a durable fix.

—Mike Conway
CTO, Acme Robotics
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Conway <mike@acme.com>, Kate Morris <kate@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 5xx + high latency from streaming since SDK v1.4.2

Mike / Kate — short status and actions:

1) Toggle for your tenant: YES. We can enable a defensive header reassembly fallback for Acme within 2 hours. This setting will make the streaming path accept fragmented chunk headers and avoid dropping frames while we finalize the safe parser change. Impact: small CPU overhead on streaming nodes for your tenant only.

2) Hotfix timeline: Engineering will ship the conservative reassembly patch to canary within 6 hours and to prod within 24 hours. Monica and Neha will own verification and telemetry.

3) Rollback: If you'd rather, we can force a tenant-level downgrade to the previous server runtime that uses the older distribution of streaming code; rollback would be slower (~6 hours) and is more disruptive than the targeted toggle.

Immediate next steps I'm executing now:
- Enabling tenant-level fallback for Acme (2h ETA).
- Monica will post a small npm/sha advisory for clients recommending either: a) revert to v1.4.1 or b) ensure the parser treats incoming frame chunks as byte arrays (not trimmed strings).
- I'll open a shared incident doc and invite your on-call: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/repro/INF-4821 (editing access granted).

I'll update you the moment the toggle is live. Apologies for the disruption — we'll get this stabilized fast.

—Marcus Lin
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
